title: Expose the exact Paper settlement persistence bottleneck without changing settlement behavior
author: agent:/root

scope.goal: First bounded step on the accepted highest-priority settlement latency work: identify which existing persistence phase consumes time, without claiming a speedup or changing accounting/transaction behavior before that evidence exists.
inScope: Only the existing PaperSettlementProcessor -> IAppRepository.PersistPaperPositionSettlementBatchAsync -> PostgresAppRepository settlement-batch call path.

Add per-attempt monotonic elapsed-time diagnostics for batch preparation/serialization, connection acquisition, transaction start, wallet advisory locks, position-row locks, position upsert, settlement insert, commit and resource disposal, distinguishing completed from failed/incomplete stages.

Extend existing settlement completion, deadlock-retry and failure logs with measured persistence stage durations and the last/slowest stage; preserve current log levels, warning threshold and existing fields. No per-position log stream.

Source-compatible optional stage-aware repository path; old callers and repositories without phase support retain existing behavior and report unavailable diagnostics rather than invented zero timings.

Focused tests, bounded documentation and independent review. Tests may use a dedicated disposable PostgreSQL instance/database under the managed D:\CodexTemp lifecycle; never Production or the user's application Local database.
outOfScope: An immediate latency reduction claim, speculative SQL optimization, changing SQL statements, their parameters/order, wallet/position lock semantics, transaction boundaries, isolation, retries, queue order, scheduling, worker counts or the updater semaphore.
Copied-performance queue optimization, Dashboard reconciliation repair, Binance freshness rules or any of the other three proposed workstreams.
Changing strategies, execution intents, Paper/Live orders/fills/settlements/accounting formulas, balances, fees, PnL, historical data, Maker-GTD semantics or exception classification.
Production writes, schema/index/trigger changes, backups, deployment, server/service stop or restart; user-controlled deployment remains separate.
scope.periodOrFilter: Future Paper settlement batches after user-controlled deployment. Evidence case: 2026-09-11T05:22:36.214Z, condition0xa26f43714ea4ee229c32bbb49ade9bc63ce4b2497d5c7e649a365137f985f693,165positions/165settlements,total2905.7368ms,persistence2831.4276ms; no historical replay.
scope.firstVerification: Inspect actual batch SQL/lock path and focused tests, compare it with deployed a3f92a7ce79300672d94ef191a9c473e4f99b839, and verify the exact server-log case before product edits. Those read-only checks found existing bulk SQL and no internal persistence-stage timing, so the SQL bottleneck is still unknown.

requirements.text: Expose measured internal settlement persistence stages so the next optimization is based on the real bottleneck rather than the aggregate PersistenceDurationMs span.
acceptanceCriteria: Each attempt reports nonnegative elapsed durations from a monotonic timer, actual entered/failed stage, slowest observed stage and availability; attempts and simultaneous batches do not share timing state.

Instrumentation separates client preparation/serialization, OpenConnection, BeginTransaction, wallet locks, position-row locks, position upsert execution, settlement insert execution, Commit and cleanup/disposal at their existing execution boundaries. Execute timings are end-to-end command durations, not claims of pure server CPU or lock-wait time.

Existing structured settlement completion/retry/failure records contain the diagnostics, with condition/asset/count/attempt correlation retained. Partial/error attempts are not presented as successful measurements; unavailable stages are not fabricated as zeros.

There are no additional SQL round trips, catalog/statistics probes, database tables, new background workers or per-position log lines. Diagnostic payloads contain stage names/durations/counts, not wallet lists, connection strings, secrets, full JSON or financial payloads.

verification.command: Run the focused PaperSettlementProcessorTests and StorageTests in Release using managed D:\CodexTemp build/test paths; inspect structured completion, retry and failure fields with controlled delayed/failing stage tests.
verification.expected: Stage attribution, availability, completed/incomplete measurements, per-attempt reset and old-interface compatibility pass; no extra SQL/financial logging introduced.
verification.evidence: Read-only evidence only: server log polycopytrader-service-20260911_029.log line91086 has Load2.6134ms,Prepare0.0732ms,Persistence2831.4276ms,Cache71.6216ms,total2905.7368ms. Source already performs wallet/row locking and two bulk writes before commit; no internal stage identifies the bottleneck yet.

requirements.text: Keep the existing settlement result and concurrency behavior unchanged while adding diagnostics.
acceptanceCriteria: Existing overloads remain usable. An empty batch returns0 without opening a connection; repositories without telemetry support retain their existing persistence implementation.

The actual SQL, parameters, lock order, single transaction, duplicate settlement ON CONFLICT behavior and returned inserted count remain unchanged. No splitting the atomic settlement batch and no early exposure-cache updates.

Successful batches keep identical ledger/zeroed positions; replay keeps prior ledger and returns0. Failure/cancellation rolls back as before; diagnostic collection cannot turn committed success into a business failure/retry or replace the original persistence exception.

Deadlock retry still uses the existing maximum3 attempts and reloads current positions before retry; non-deadlock errors and cancellation remain unchanged. The cache is updated only after successful persistence; stale marks cannot restore a settled position.

Focused PostgreSQL tests actually execute against an isolated disposable test target; a missing test connection/early return is not represented as a passing integration verification. No Production or application Local DB is used.

verification.command: Run focused PaperSettlementPostgresIntegrationTests, PaperSettlementProcessorTests and PaperTradingMarketDataUpdaterQueueTests in Release with explicit isolated disposable PostgreSQL test target and D:\CodexTemp artifacts/results; compare actual SQL before/after the diff.
verification.expected: Exact stages and delayed lock/command attribution verified together with original accounting, rollback, replay, same-wallet coordination, cancellation/deadlock and stale-mark invariants; no statement/order/transaction semantic change.
verification.evidence: Existing tests inspected include SettlementBatch_FiltersMarketAndRollsBackBothTablesOnFailure, same-wallet singleton/batch contention, ConditionalMarkUpdates_DoNotRestoreSettledPositions and processor deadlock/cancellation tests. No tests or database mutations executed in draft phase.
